content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; cap upward spikes or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >75) by forecasting further increases; apply mean reversion bias if price >75 and sentiment <0.5.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum followed by a drop, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope after sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is high; apply downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points if sentiment >0.7.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add small upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often misses mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average if sentiment remains flat.
